reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is a defensible stance and MARKET_VOLUME is correctly named: the only volume figure is a RECOMMENDATION ('probably about 2,000 mobile signings a month' in the metro), which is an estimate of a category total shared among many signing services, not a count of reachable title companies or of this seller's order volume; 20 signings x $150 = $3,000 at the 15% measured rate needs about 134 contacts (20 / 0.15 = 133.3), and nothing shows that many reachable buyers or enough repeat orders. But the revision treats price as EVIDENCED when it is not established for this buyer: the card's price fact is 'three published signing-service fee schedules', i.e. what other signing services list as their charge. That is a benchmark of what someone else charges, not a purchase price these title companies are shown paying for this offer; the 9/60 agreements on the card carry no price. So the no-plan omits a second decisive link, and its resolution ('if the roster count is enough, re-plan as executable through SignRight at $75') is wrong: even with the roster counted, OFFER_AND_PRICE would still rest on another seller's figure, so the most the evidence could support is a CONDITIONAL plan whose live priced offer measures what these buyers pay. Economics would hold if $150 were paid (cost $75 written, exposure $0, 7 days to cash).
findings: Add OFFER_AND_PRICE to noPlan.decisiveLinks and set the price quantity to UNKNOWN (benchmark $150 from published fee schedules of other services), not EVIDENCED.

Rewrite the resolution: research the roster count and order frequency (MARKET_VOLUME), then a live priced offer at $150 to establish OFFER_AND_PRICE (a CONDITIONAL plan with proof/stop/continue), rather than re-planning straight to EXECUTABLE.
The 9/60 agreements should state the price agreed; if they were at $150 that would establish the price on this offer's own record and remove the second gap, but the card does not say so.
Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis says 19 deals needed; at $150, 19 x $150 = $2,850 < $3,000, so 20 is correct as the revision states.

conditions.why: The price fact is three published signing-service fee schedules: what other services charge, not a price these title companies are shown paying for this offer. A benchmark is not this buyer's purchase price.

reviews.reasons: I re-examined the rebuttal against the card. MARKET_VOLUME remains correctly named as the decisive gap and NO_PLAN remains the right stance today. The disagreement is OFFER_AND_PRICE. The price fact's own words are 'three published signing-service fee schedules': those are the rates signing services publish as what they charge. A published fee schedule is a seller's list price, i.e. a benchmark of what someone else charges; it is not a record of these title companies paying $150 to this offer, and nothing on this offer's own record (the 9/60 agreements carry no price) shows that. Brain's OFFER_AND_PRICE basis is 'price 150 USD (EVIDENCE)', not this offer's own sales, so the contradicting record is the price fact itself. Agreement among three sellers' schedules shows the market rate is consistent, which makes $150 a reasonable offer price, but it is still not a purchase price these buyers are shown paying a new provider. The revised resolution still re-plans to EXECUTABLE once the roster is counted at 'the established $150 rate', and its first-batch check measures only the close rate. The fix is small: name OFFER_AND_PRICE alongside MARKET_VOLUME (or as the link the first batch decides), and make the first outreach batch a priced proof: paid or signed orders at $150 from title companies, with a stop rule that re-plans on the price actually paid. Arithmetic is otherwise correct: 20 x $150 = $3,000; 20 / 0.15 = 134 contacts; margin $75 per signing at SignRight's written rate; exposure $0; 7 days to cash.
findings: The price quantity is labelled 'what title companies pay signing services': that is a market benchmark from sellers' published schedules, so it should be marked as a benchmark rate (offer price), not as an evidenced purchase price for this offer.

Resolution: after the roster count, the plan can at most be CONDITIONAL with validation.decides = OFFER_AND_PRICE (proof: N paid/signed signings at $150 from the first batch by a named day; stop: fewer than N, re-plan on the price buyers actually accept; continue: work the rest of the roster). This is cheap (the first batch is outreach the plan already includes) and removes the unproven assumption.
If the 9 agreements on the card were in fact at $150, record that price on the conversion fact: it would establish OFFER_AND_PRICE on this offer's own record and settle the dispute without a test.

conditions.why: The price fact cites three published signing-service fee schedules: sellers' list prices, a benchmark of what others charge, not a record of these title companies paying $150 for this offer. No agreement or payment on this offer's own record carries a price.

The resolution is now actionable and safe: research the land-title association roster count and order frequency, then re-plan through SignRight at its written $75 (margin $75, exposure $0, 7 days to cash) with the first outreach batch as a priced proof (at least 3 signed or paid signings at $150 from the first 20 contacts by day 7; fewer stops and re-plans on the price and close rate actually observed). That proof is exactly the live test my earlier condition asked for, so the owner will not be committed to $150 before these buyers have accepted it. Nothing unknown is treated as known in what the plan does now (one research step, no spend).
